text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 2.1% today, continuing a steady climb over the past week as crude oil prices pushed higher following U.S. military strikes against Iran. The price of crude hit $90 per barrel, and with refineries running at 97.4% capacity, tight supply conditions are supporting margins for refiners like Marathon—the company profits when it can buy crude and sell refined products like gasoline at a favorable spread.

The broader backdrop matters too: Middle East tensions are driving oil prices up, while geopolitical moves like Venezuela opening new oil fields to U.S. firms add uncertainty to global supply. For a refiner, higher crude prices can cut both ways, but when refineries are running near full capacity as they are now, the company has pricing power on the products it sells, which appears to be supporting the stock's upward trend this week.
